$comment: Command Governor component manifest and pin record (ADR 0009 §11).
This file is the single source of truth for which runtime substrate the
distribution targets; nothing else may hardcode a version string.
Prime Agent is not published to the npm registry. Its wrapper package
declares its three sibling packages as bare URLs on a Cloudflare R2 bucket
with no integrity hash, so a URL is never a pin here. Every release asset
is recorded by name, sha256 (matching the release's own SHA256SUMS) and
sha512 (the npm integrity form the lockfile enforces). scripts/bootstrap.sh
downloads the assets from the immutable GitHub release, verifies both
hashes against this record before npm is allowed to run, and refuses to
proceed if pins/SHA256SUMS and this record disagree.
Prime republishes upstream Pi's package names (@earendil-works/pi-agent-core,
pi-ai, pi-tui) at its own 0.8.1 line. One node_modules tree cannot hold
both Pi 0.84.4 and Prime 0.8.1, so the upstream-Pi fallback below is a
record, never a co-install; the conformance suite asserts the install root
contains no @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent.
Third-party package policy (packages[]): an entry MUST carry either an
exact npm version (exactVersion) or a 40-character git commit SHA
(resolvedSha), a license, a review date and the authority it owns. A bare
name, a branch, or a tag is not a pin and the conformance suite rejects it.

substrate.name: prime-agent
substrate.commitNote: Tag v0.8.1 resolves to this commit; verified via the GitHub API during Gate S0 (Issue #15) and again when this manifest was written.
substrate.licenseNote: MIT License, Copyright (c) 2025 Mario Zechner, Copyright (c) 2026 Prime Intellect (LICENSE at the pinned commit). No distribution restriction blocks shipping it as the substrate.

requirements.python: CPython 3.11 via uv, bootstrapped lazily on first tool use into <agentDir>/kernel-venv (~270 MB, network required). Not needed by the credential-free conformance tier, which never triggers a tool call.
requirements.network: GitHub release download at bootstrap; npm registry for transitive dependencies; R2 mirror for the three sibling tarballs (bytes verified against the sha512 above).
requirements.installScripts: ignored (npm ci --ignore-scripts). Prime's postinstall is a no-op unless PRIME_AGENT_BOOTSTRAP_* opt-ins are set; zeromq and koffi ship prebuilt binaries for darwin-arm64 and linux-x64.

authority.processes: detached supervisor plus one resident worker process per root session (each may spawn a Python kernel and bash subprocesses)
authority.filesystem: <agentDir> (sessions, daemon-workers, session-leases, session-artifacts, rlm-ledger, logs, kernel-venv) and <TMPDIR>/prime-agent-<uid>/ for Unix sockets
authority.network: model providers as configured; telemetry disabled by the Governor (PRIME_AGENT_TELEMETRY=0)
authority.credentials: create/attach forward launchEnv to the supervisor and worker; the Governor client sends a positive allowlist only (governor/prime/env.ts)

substrate.updatePolicy: Re-pin only through docs/prime-distribution.md's ritual: new tag -> commit verified via API -> assets downloaded and hashed -> pins.json, pins/SHA256SUMS and the install-root lockfile updated together -> scripts/conformance.sh green locally AND in the merge-gating harness job -> independent re-run of D1/D2/D8.
substrate.conformance: scripts/conformance.sh (Tier 1 credential-free, including the runtime tier under conformance/runtime that drives the pinned daemon in isolation).
substrate.reviewedBy: docs/research/2026-09-01-agent-harness-landscape-and-substrate-bakeoff.md; Issue #15 (Gate S0/S1 real-machine evidence); Issue #17 (this adaptation layer)

fallback.$comment: Recorded, not installed. ADR 0009 §2 names upstream Pi v0.84.4 as the first fallback if Prime fails; frozen PR #16 carries the working bootstrap for it.
